reverse_expectations.method: Hold year-1 revenue at $2.35B, Base margin path 22% to 24%, required return at 9% and terminal multiple at 22x; solve constant revenue growth for years 2-10 that equates model value to the reference price.
reverse_expectations.interpretation: Conditional expectation set, not a unique market forecast.

two_state_note: Mechanical weight only; not a real-world probability estimate.
valuation_judgment: At $160.31 the stock is roughly at the unchanged Base value rather than meaningfully below it. The reverse model requires approximately 18.2% annual revenue growth for nine years under a 22%-24% owner-cash margin path and 22x terminal multiple. Given current triple-digit growth this is feasible, but customer concentration, acquisition integration, SBC and terminal-value dependence leave inadequate margin of safety for STARTER.
